_comment: Y4/G4 hand-verified .eml fixture corpus. Every count below was fixed BEFORE mail-parser was invoked against any of these files, by (1) hand-authoring the raw RFC 5322/MIME bytes (build_mail_fixtures.py, referenced from SPIKE-G4.md) so the author already knows the answer, and (2) independently cross-checking with Python's stdlib `email` package (verify_with_stdlib_email.py) -- a different implementation from both the author's own arithmetic and from mail-parser. Only after both agreed was mail-parser run once, diagnostically, to compare (transcript in SPIKE-G4.md gate (b)). counting_rules defines what each field counts, precisely enough that a human can open a fixture in a text editor and reach the same number without knowing anything about mail-parser's own vocabulary.

counting_rules.header_count: Number of distinct top-level RFC 5322 header field LINES at the outermost message envelope (the block above the first blank line), counted by eye as one line = one field; no field in this corpus is folded across multiple lines or repeated, so line count and field count are identical. Sub-headers inside a MIME part (e.g. a part's own Content-Type) are NOT counted here -- see mime_leaf_part_count for those.
counting_rules.to_address_count: Number of individual mailbox addresses in the To: header, counting each comma-separated mailbox once (a display-name + angle-addr pair is one address).
counting_rules.cc_address_count: Same rule as to_address_count, applied to Cc:. 0 when there is no Cc: header.
counting_rules.mime_leaf_part_count: Number of MIME body parts with no further sub-parts (a multipart/* container itself is not counted, only its leaves). A message with no explicit multipart structure (a bare Content-Type: text/plain message) counts as 1.
counting_rules.attachment_count: Number of leaf MIME parts carrying Content-Disposition: attachment (with a filename parameter). A nested message/rfc822 part is counted here too when it also carries Content-Disposition: attachment, per the wave brief's own framing ("an attachment that is a message/rfc822 is a nested message") -- nested_message_count below identifies which attachment(s), if any, are that case.
counting_rules.nested_message_count: Number of leaf MIME parts whose Content-Type is exactly message/rfc822.
counting_rules.body_text_present: true iff at least one leaf part has Content-Type text/plain and non-empty decoded content.
counting_rules.body_html_present: true iff at least one leaf part has Content-Type text/html and non-empty decoded content in the SOURCE bytes (see SPIKE-G4.md gate (b) note: mail-parser synthesizes an HTML alternative from a plain-text body when none exists in the source -- this field describes the wire bytes, not mail-parser's post-parse output).
counting_rules.attachment_decoded_byte_len: The exact length, in bytes, of an attachment's DECODED content (after undoing its Content-Transfer-Encoding), not the length of the encoded (e.g. base64) text in the wire bytes.
counting_rules.subject_decoded: The Subject header's value after RFC 2047 encoded-word decoding, exactly as the author's original plaintext (used as the encoder's input, per the wave brief's requirement that a human reading the fixture can reach the same answer -- here, by decoding the encoded-word by hand or checking build_mail_fixtures.py's recorded plaintext).
counting_rules.from_display_decoded: The From header's display-name after RFC 2047 decoding, same rule as subject_decoded.
counting_rules.body_charset_declared: The charset= parameter on the relevant text/plain part's Content-Type header, as written in the wire bytes (not mail-parser's interpretation of it).
counting_rules.valid: false means: the ONLY passing outcome for a parser is refusal to produce a Message (mail-parser: parse() returns None) -- any Message at all, partial or otherwise, is a failure of this fixture, per the wave brief's malformed-message requirement.

fixtures.covers: Plain text message, no MIME multipart structure
multipart/alternative with both text and HTML bodies

Report body line one.
Report body line two.

fixtures.covers: Nested message/rfc822 (a mail inside a mail)

nested_message.body_text_decoded: This is the original message text, now nested one level deep.

fixtures.covers: Encoding zoo: quoted-printable body, base64 attachment, RFC 2047 encoded Subject (UTF-8 B-encoding) and From display-name (ISO-8859-1 Q-encoding), non-UTF-8 body charset (windows-1252)
Deliberately malformed message that MUST fail rather than parse partially -- no RFC 5322 header field line anywhere in the file, so a conformant parser has zero headers to recover
fixtures.required_outcome: Parser refuses to produce a Message (mail-parser: MessageParser::parse() returns None, per its own documented contract -- "a best-effort is made to parse the message, and if no headers are found, None is returned", docs.rs/mail-parser/0.11.8). Any Message at all -- including one with zero body units -- is a failure of this fixture.

diagnostic_not_in_manifest.purpose: NOT part of the exact-match corpus above and asserts nothing (same status as Y2's fixture 06 hostile-expansion file). A well-formed RFC 5322 envelope (valid From/To/Subject/Date/Message-ID/MIME-Version/Content-Type, 7 headers) whose declared multipart boundary is never closed (no --BROKEN-- terminator, no second --BROKEN). Recorded because it produced a materially different mail-parser outcome than fixture 06 -- see SPIKE-G4.md gate (b), 'A caveat found empirically' -- and that finding needed a byte record, not just prose.
